newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower despite harvest slowdown.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower despite harvest slowdown.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower despite rain-slowed soy harvesting with technical sell stops driving November below key support at the $7.00 per bushel level, traders said.
"It was fund selling," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Refco Inc sold at least seven million bushels in the January, Griffin Trading sold 3.5 million January and bought three million November, and Prudential Securities sold 2.5 million bushels of January, traders said.
Commercial action also was noted.
Cargill Inc sold five million bushels of January, and Continental Grain bear spread three million March/January and did 2.5 million July/November, traders said.

Fundamentals were little changed with the market continuing to operate under the umbrella of a relatively large USDA-estimated 2.346 billion bushel soybean crop now being harvested in the U.S. Midwest, the traders said.
Farmer selling patterns were noted but prospects for that activity remained cloudy.
Soybeans closed 3-3/4 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with November down 3-3/4 at $6.98-1/2.
"Farmer selling is slow but everyone knows there is a large crop out there and it has to come to market sometime," a trader said.

Nearby November again moved to an inverse with the January on the slow farmer selling pace and there were some ideas producer sales may slow even further. An Internal Revenue Service tax memorandum recently circulated could raise farmer's 1996 income taxes and shift delivery of soybeans into the January forward positions, Lespinasse said.

Soybeans in late trading showed signs of buoyancy with the market near the close retracing nearly 50 percent of the daily losses. Late local short covering brought the market up from the day's lows, the traders said.
"It got too short. It's plain and simple, they were just too short and (they) covered," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor of the late resiliency in the soy complex.
Technicians said the key moving averages remained bearish.

But short term technical indicators were sagging to near oversold levels with November's nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing at 39.999 points. Technicians generally consider an RSI of 30 or less a sign of an oversold market.
The market shrugged off rainy weather in the U.S. Midwest which slowed soybean harvesting.
USDA Monday said 73 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was harvested as of Sunday, below the low end of trader expectations for 75 to 80 percent.
A year ago, 85 percent of the crop had been combined and the five-year average for U.S. soybean harvest completion was 81 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 65,000, down from 68,332 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services sold 700 March $7.00 calls at 25 to 25-1/2 cents, Refco Inc bought 350 January $6.75 puts at 8-1/2 cents and First American sold 200 January $6.75 puts at 8-8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 11,000, up from 7,497 Monday.
